current_row.boundary_rationale: This unit opens at the hoy onset web:Isa.33.1, “Woe to you who destroy, but you weren't destroyed, and who betray, but nobody betrayed you! When you have finished destroying, you will be destroyed; and when you have finished betrayal, you will be betrayed.”, pointed ה֣וֹי שׁוֹדֵ֗ד וְאַתָּה֙ לֹ֣א שָׁד֔וּד וּבוֹגֵ֖ד וְלֹא בָ֣גְדוּ ב֑וֹ כַּהֲתִֽמְךָ֤ שׁוֹדֵד֙ תּוּשַּׁ֔ד כַּנְּלֹתְךָ֥ לִבְגֹּ֖ד יִבְגְּדוּ בָֽךְ (oshb:Isa.33.1, tier: byte), the sixth hoy onset within the chapters 28-33 span (sweep: 6 verses). This same onset, oshb:Isa.33.1, is itself marked by a parashah SAMEKH mark (single-witness), and a further SAMEKH mark (single-witness) closes the preceding verse, oshb:Isa.32.20, immediately ahead of it. The unit runs through web:Isa.33.24 as one woe-framed liturgy complex: the communal petition יְהוָ֥ה חָנֵּ֖נוּ (oshb:Isa.33.2, byte tier), “Yahweh, be gracious to us.” (web:Isa.33.2), a divine-name vocative followed by an imperative; the presentative הֵ֚ן אֶרְאֶלָּ֔ם (oshb:Isa.33.7, byte tier), verse-initial at one of only two sites of that presentative across chapters 28-35 (the other being the coming-king onset of a neighboring unit); and the summons שִׁמְע֥וּ רְחוֹקִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֑יתִי (oshb:Isa.33.13, byte tier), that imperative verse-initial at exactly 10 verses book-wide and at this single site across chapters 28-35, the same formal class as the summons opening web:Isa.34.1 -- all three continue addressing the same scene the woe opens rather than turning to a new one, and none carries a fresh hoy, massa, or divine-frame marker of its own; it is that absence, not the absence of any interior imperative or vocative whatsoever, that keeps the complex bounded as one unit through web:Isa.33.24. Two further SAMEKH marks (single-witness), interior to the unit, fall at oshb:Isa.33.6 and oshb:Isa.33.12, marking internal stanza turns that bind to no fresh hoy or vocative marker of their own. A postpositive amar-Yahweh signature at oshb:Isa.33.10, עַתָּ֥ה אָק֖וּם יֹאמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה עַתָּה֙ אֵֽרוֹמָ֔ם עַתָּ֖ה אֶנָּשֵֽׂא (tier: byte), identifies the speaker within the continuing complex rather than opening a narrative or messenger-formula frame of its own. A paseq mark (single-witness) sits at oshb:Isa.33.14, tallying presence rather than placement.

items.adjudicator_grounds: Every byte ground re-derives. The summons שִׁמְע֥וּ רְחוֹקִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֑יתִי (oshb:Isa.33.13, byte tier) is a verse-initial imperative with named addressees; that verse-initial imperative stands at exactly 10 MT verses book-wide, identical at skeleton and accent-stripped tiers (MT 1:2, 1:10, 33:13, 46:3, 46:12, 48:1, 49:1, 51:1, 51:7, 66:5), MT 33:13 the single chapters-28-35 site. The seg layer carries SAMEKH at MT 33:1, 33:6, 33:12. Under the convention this corpus itself applies -- the row reads the MT 32:20 seg as closing the preceding verse -- the MT 33:12 division falls immediately before the summons, so the row's claim that its interior segs mark turns binding 'to no fresh hoy or vocative marker of their own' is byte-false at exactly the declined site; it is true only at MT 33:6, whose next verse opens on the presentative הֵ֚ן אֶרְאֶלָּ֔ם (oshb:Isa.33.7, byte tier). The stated decline rule -- absence of a fresh hoy, massa, or divine-frame marker -- also fails to discriminate MT 33:13 from קִרְב֤וּ גוֹיִם֙ לִשְׁמֹ֔עַ וּלְאֻמִּ֖ים הַקְשִׁ֑יבוּ (oshb:Isa.34.1, byte tier): first-token and koh-amar-bigram checks at skeleton tier find no hoy, massa, or koh-amar frame in either onset, the row itself calls the two the same formal class, and the neighbouring row cuts at MT 34:1; on the row's stated rule its own rear seam at MT 33:24, which carries no seg, is left without positive warrant. A whole-chapter span held by a decline that omits the tier-1 imperative-onset and addressee-shift class and rests on a byte-false mark-binding claim is a load-bearing defect: high as filed. Span ruling: endorse_proposal -- the respan case is byte-sound (a tier-1 summons onset at MT 33:13, the same signal class the sibling cuts at MT 32:9 and MT 34:1 rest on, with the MT 33:12 SAMEKH as tier-3 corroboration), and the proposal's alternative branch, holding the span under a re-argued decline that does distinguish MT 34:1's scene turn from the continuing Zion scene at MT 33:13-14, stays open to the owner docket; nothing adopted here.

readjudication.grounds: Re-derived from bytes, both sides. (1) The filed digits hold: the verse-initial imperative of שִׁמְע֥וּ רְחוֹקִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֑יתִי (oshb:Isa.33.13, tier: byte) stands verse-initial at exactly 10 MT verses book-wide, identical at skeleton and accent-stripped tiers (sweep: 10 verses, verse-initial token: MT 1:2, 1:10, 33:13, 46:3, 46:12, 48:1, 49:1, 51:1, 51:7, 66:5), one site in chs 28-35; the verse-initial hoy of ה֣וֹי שׁוֹדֵ֗ד (oshb:Isa.33.1, tier: byte) is the sixth of the chs 28-33 woe series (sweep: 6 verses, verse-initial token at skeleton tier: MT 28:1, 29:1, 29:15, 30:1, 31:1, 33:1); the single-witness inventory carries SAMEKH at MT 33:1, 33:6 and 33:12 and nothing at 33:24, so the row's claim that its interior segs mark turns binding to no fresh vocative marker is byte-false at 33:12, whose division falls immediately before the summons, and true only at 33:6, whose next verse opens on the presentative הֵ֚ן אֶרְאֶלָּ֔ם (oshb:Isa.33.7, tier: byte). (2) Characterization, as instructed: the defect is INADEQUATE TREATMENT, not total omission -- the row quotes the 33:13 summons at byte tier, verifies its digit, names its formal class as that of the summons opening 34:1, and then declines it on a rule (no fresh hoy, massa or divine-frame marker) that omits the ruled imperative/vocative-summons and addressee-shift class and that, as stated, cannot discriminate 33:13 from קִרְב֤וּ גוֹיִם֙ לִשְׁמֹ֔עַ וּלְאֻמִּ֖ים הַקְשִׁ֑יבוּ (oshb:Isa.34.1, tier: byte), which carries no hoy, no massa and no koh-amar frame either (first-token and formula sweeps at skeleton tier) yet opens the neighbouring row; its scene-continuity sentence is asserted, not shown from bytes. (3) Both-sides test at the declined seam MT 33:12|33:13: the preceding side closes on וְהָי֥וּ עַמִּ֖ים מִשְׂרְפ֣וֹת שִׂ֑יד (oshb:Isa.33.12, tier: byte), third-person description whose runs stand at exactly 1 verse book-wide at skeleton tier -- no refrain, no formula, so the refrain-close rule (§6) gives no close-side warrant and the SAMEKH there is tier-3 corroboration only. The onset side carries the ruled summons class (§2a: verse-initial imperative with the named addressees רְחוֹקִ֖ים and קְרוֹבִ֖ים), and the addressee does change in the bytes: 33:11 addresses a second-person plural, רוּחֲכֶ֕ם אֵ֖שׁ תֹּאכַלְכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.33.11, tier: byte), 33:12 is third-person, 33:13 summons the far and the near. The seam is therefore warranted from its onset side and the row's stated decline ground fails. (4) The ground the row could have argued and did not: the summons is bound to the divine speech opened by the postpositive signature עַתָּ֥ה אָק֖וּם יֹאמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Isa.33.10, tier: byte) through its own first-person forms עָשִׂ֑יתִי and גְּבֻרָתִֽי (oshb:Isa.33.13, tier: byte; both witnesses render first person; no morphology layer is staged), and the speaker changes only at פָּחֲד֤וּ בְצִיּוֹן֙ חַטָּאִ֔ים with מִ֣י יָג֣וּר לָ֗נוּ (oshb:Isa.33.14, tier: byte), a first-person-plural community voice; 34:1's summons carries no first-person form and continues no frame, its preceding verse וּבַל יֹאמַ֥ר שָׁכֵ֖ן חָלִ֑יתִי (oshb:Isa.33.24, tier: byte) closing in third-person description. That ground survives the tier-1 class and discriminates 33:13 from 34:1 under the frame-plus-speech default (§6). Severity: the prior adjudication confirmed high on the rule that a whole-chapter span held by a decline omitting the tier-1 class and resting on a byte-false mark-binding claim is load-bearing, on the premise that the respan is byte-sound; the complete test shows the boundary is not byte-shown wrong (a sound hold-warrant exists in the bytes, and the rear seam at 33:24 is warranted from the following unit's onset at 34:1, the ruled addressee shift to the nations), the byte-false binding claim concerns a tier-3 layer that can bear no boundary load under owner law, and the load-bearing defect is a wrongly stated decline rule: a defective warrant on a byte-sound span -- downgrade to medium. Span ruling: decline_proposal on the respan branch -- a cut at 33:12|33:13 would sever the first-person divine speech MT 33:10-13 from its own closing summons with no ruled close on the preceding side; the proposal's hold-and-re-argue branch is the remedy the bytes support and is a field repair, not a span change; a rival interior cut at the speaker shift 33:13|33:14 is disclosed as a docket question, not ruled here. Ruled coherently with the 34:1 row, whose onset stands (verse-initial imperative at exactly 3 verses book-wide at skeleton tier: MT 34:1, 41:21, 48:16).

current_row.boundary_rationale: This unit opens the assigned narrative range at web:Isa.36.1, “Now in the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria attacked all of the fortified cities of Judah and captured them.” (web:Isa.36.1), a chronological narration-onset naming the fourteenth year of Hezekiah and Sennacherib's campaign against Judah's fortified cities, in Hebrew וַיְהִ֡י בְּאַרְבַּע֩ עֶשְׂרֵ֨ה שָׁנָ֜ה לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֗הוּ עָלָ֞ה סַנְחֵרִ֤יב מֶֽלֶךְ אַשּׁוּר֙ עַ֣ל כָּל עָרֵ֧י יְהוּדָ֛ה הַבְּצֻר֖וֹת וַֽיִּתְפְּשֵֽׂם (oshb:Isa.36.1, tier: byte). The scene continues through the Assyrian king's own royal messenger reaching Jerusalem's aqueduct and closes with Judah's delegation coming out to meet him at web:Isa.36.3, “Then Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah, the son of Asaph the recorder came out to him.” (web:Isa.36.3), naming Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah by office. Immediately ahead of this unit's own onset, oshb:Isa.35.10 carries a parashah PE mark (single-witness) that closes the preceding oracle rather than anything inside this narrative-zone unit. The following verse opens the Rabshakeh's own royal-messenger speech with a fresh frame formula, and this row's own close at the delegation's arrival does not cross into that speech.

current_row.boundary_rationale: This short unit turns on an audience question rather than on a new speech frame: at web:Isa.36.11, “Then Eliakim, Shebna and Joah said to Rabshakeh, “Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, for we understand it. Don’t speak to us in the Jews’ language in the hearing of the people who are on the wall.”” (web:Isa.36.11), the officials ask the Rabshakeh to switch languages so the people on the wall cannot follow; the request for Aramaic is narrated STORY CONTENT here, not a label on the verse's own language, which remains Hebrew throughout the staged extract. The Rabshakeh's refusal follows at web:Isa.36.12, “But Rabshakeh said, “Has my master sent me only to your master and to you, to speak these words, and not to the men who sit on the wall, who will eat their own dung and drink their own urine with you?”” (web:Isa.36.12), in Hebrew וַיֹּ֣אמֶר רַב שָׁקֵ֗ה הַאֶ֨ל אֲדֹנֶ֤יךָ וְאֵלֶ֨יךָ֙ שְׁלָחַ֣נִי אֲדֹנִ֔י לְדַבֵּ֖ר אֶת הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה הֲלֹ֣א עַל הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים הַיֹּֽשְׁבִים֙ עַל הַ֣חוֹמָ֔ה לֶאֱכֹ֣ל אֶת חראיהם צוֹאָתָ֗ם וְלִשְׁתּ֛וֹת אֶת שיניהם מֵימֵ֥י רַגְלֵיהֶ֖ם עִמָּכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.36.12, tier: byte), itself a doubled ketiv/qere verse (single-witness apparatus) and the site where the Rabshakeh's own title again surfaces as two separate tokens rather than one compound word, visible in the same pointed quote above. The same verse carries two distinct adonai-family forms rather than one form repeated: the second-person-singular-suffixed אֲדֹנֶ֤יךָ (oshb:Isa.36.12, tier: byte) and the first-person-singular-suffixed אֲדֹנִ֔י (oshb:Isa.36.12, tier: byte), distinct from each other at byte tier and at finals-normalized skeleton tier alike; only the second is a member of the book's bare hiriq-pointed adonai census, which stands at exactly three verses (MT 36:8, 36:9, 36:12). Both tokens name the human master relation rather than the divine title. This row closes with the Rabshakeh's own crude threat, before he turns to address the wider audience directly in the next unit.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: An alternative fold of this two-verse exchange into the surrounding Rabshakeh speech does not hold: the delegates' own request and the Rabshakeh's refusal turn on the audience question itself, a scene concern distinct from either flanking taunt. The frame-plus-speech default would instead keep the whole 36:4-20 complex as one continuous royal-messenger unit, an architecture this row's own addressee-question boundary argues against.

readjudication.grounds: Re-derived from bytes, both sides of the front seam MT 36:10|36:11. Preceding side: the prior unit closes on the herald's own YHWH-attribution יְהוָה֙ אָמַ֣ר אֵלַ֔י עֲלֵ֛ה (oshb:Isa.36.10, tier: byte), a rhetorical close standing at exactly 1 verse book-wide at skeleton tier -- no refrain, no formula close, and no seg at MT 36:10 or 36:11 in the single-witness inventory (absence not counterevidence); the refrain-close rule (§6) offers nothing, so the seam depends on its onset side. Onset side: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶלְיָקִים֩ וְשֶׁבְנָ֨א וְיוֹאָ֜ח אֶל רַב שָׁקֵ֗ה (oshb:Isa.36.11, tier: byte; the title is two tokens in the staged extract) is a verse-initial narrative speech frame with full speaker-and-addressee inversion against the frame that opened the prior unit, וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶם֙ רַב שָׁקֵ֔ה (oshb:Isa.36.4, tier: byte) -- the ruled participant/scene-shift class at which narrative_prose units cut (§6); verse-initial vayomer stands at 10 MT verses in chs 36-39 (sweep: 10 verses, verse-initial token at skeleton tier: 36:4, 36:11, 36:12, 37:6, 38:3, 38:21, 38:22, 39:4, 39:5, 39:8) and the 36:11 speaker set is unique (sweep: 1 verse, the four-token onset at skeleton tier). current_row.boundary_rationale: This unit opens at web:Isa.36.13, “Then Rabshakeh stood, and called out with a loud voice in the Jews’ language, and said, “Hear the words of the great king, the king of Assyria!”” (web:Isa.36.13), pointed at its onset as וַֽיַּעֲמֹד֙ רַב שָׁקֵ֔ה וַיִּקְרָ֥א בְקוֹל גָּד֖וֹל יְהוּדִ֑ית (oshb:Isa.36.13, tier: byte). The proclamation is made in a loud voice and in יְהוּדִ֑ית (oshb:Isa.36.13, tier: byte), the Judahite-language noun the verse itself carries, rather than the Aramaic the officials had just requested as narrated story content in the preceding unit; neither witness labels this proclamation 'Hebrew'. A second royal-messenger formula opens immediately at web:Isa.36.14, “The king says, ‘Don’t let Hezekiah deceive you; for he will not be able to deliver you.” (web:Isa.36.14), in Hebrew כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אַל יַשִּׁ֥א לָכֶ֖ם חִזְקִיָּ֑הוּ כִּ֥י לֹֽא יוּכַ֖ל לְהַצִּ֥יל אֶתְכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.36.14, tier: byte), and a third opens at web:Isa.36.16, “Don’t listen to Hezekiah, for the king of Assyria says, ‘Make your peace with me, and come out to me; and each of you eat from his vine, and each one from his fig tree, and each one of you drink the waters of his own cistern;” (web:Isa.36.16), in Hebrew אַֽל תִּשְׁמְע֖וּ אֶל חִזְקִיָּ֑הוּ כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֜ר הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֗וּר עֲשֽׂוּ אִתִּ֤י בְרָכָה֙ וּצְא֣וּ אֵלַ֔י וְאִכְל֤וּ אִישׁ גַּפְנוֹ֙ וְאִ֣ישׁ תְּאֵנָת֔וֹ וּשְׁת֖וּ אִ֥ישׁ מֵי בוֹרֽוֹ (oshb:Isa.36.16, tier: byte), both still spoken under the Assyrian king's own frame rather than Yahweh's; this same verse also carries a parashah SAMEKH mark (single-witness), oshb:Isa.36.16. The unit runs to its own rhetorical climax at web:Isa.36.20, “Who are they among all the gods of these countries that have delivered their country out of my hand, that Yahweh should deliver Jerusalem out of my hand?’”” (web:Isa.36.20), before the officials' silence closes the scene in the following unit.

current_row.boundary_rationale: This unit opens at web:Isa.37.1, “When King Hezekiah heard it, he tore his clothes, covered himself with sackcloth, and went into Yahweh’s house.” (web:Isa.37.1), pointed at its own onset as וַיְהִ֗י כִּשְׁמֹ֨עַ֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ (oshb:Isa.37.1, tier: byte) — a verse-initial wayehi-plus-temporal-infinitive clause naming an explicit new grammatical subject, the king himself, in place of the delegation that closes the preceding unit. That construction, verse-initial wayehi at exact token match, stands at seven verses book-wide (sweep: 7 verses), four of them in this narrative zone, oshb:Isa.36.1, oshb:Isa.37.1, oshb:Isa.37.38 and oshb:Isa.38.4, and only oshb:Isa.36.1 and this verse pair it with both a temporal frame and an explicit new subject, the same scene-onset architecture the whole narrative block itself opens with at oshb:Isa.36.1. Hezekiah then sends his own delegation to the prophet at web:Isa.37.2, “He sent Eliakim, who was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and the elders of the priests, covered with sackcloth, to Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz.” (web:Isa.37.2), Hezekiah's own sending of a sackcloth-clad delegation to Isaiah. Their message names Hezekiah's own royal-messenger frame at web:Isa.37.3, “They said to him, “Hezekiah says, ‘Today is a day of trouble, and of rebuke, and of rejection; for the children have come to the birth, and there is no strength to give birth.”” (web:Isa.37.3), in Hebrew וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֗יו כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ יוֹם צָרָ֧ה וְתוֹכֵחָ֛ה וּנְאָצָ֖ה הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה כִּ֣י בָ֤אוּ בָנִים֙ עַד מַשְׁבֵּ֔ר וְכֹ֥חַ אַ֖יִן לְלֵדָֽה (oshb:Isa.37.3, tier: byte) — that formula belongs to the king of Judah himself, not to the Assyrian king and not to Yahweh, a second frame-owner inside this same narrative zone. Isaiah's own reply opens a divine frame at web:Isa.37.6, “Isaiah said to them, “Tell your master, ‘Yahweh says, “Don’t be afraid of the words that you have heard, with which the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed me.” (web:Isa.37.6), in Hebrew וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶם֙ יְשַֽׁעְיָ֔הוּ כֹּ֥ה תֹאמְר֖וּן אֶל אֲדֹנֵיכֶ֑ם כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אַל תִּירָא֙ מִפְּנֵ֤י הַדְּבָרִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁמַ֔עְתָּ אֲשֶׁ֧ר גִּדְּפ֛וּ נַעֲרֵ֥י מֶלֶךְ אַשּׁ֖וּר אוֹתִֽי (oshb:Isa.37.6, tier: byte) — the tier-1 object distinct from both human messenger formulas already seen. The unit closes with Yahweh's own word through Isaiah at web:Isa.37.7, “Behold, I will put a spirit in him and he will hear news, and will return to his own land. I will cause him to fall by the sword in his own land.”’”” (web:Isa.37.7).
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Ending this unit at web:Isa.37.5, where the servants' own arrival before Isaiah repeats the sending already narrated at web:Isa.37.2, was considered and set aside because that repetition resumes rather than closes the single delegation scene, whose own boundary is Isaiah's answering word. A fold of web:Isa.37.1 backward into the officials' own report scene, rather than forward into Hezekiah's response, was also weighed and declined: the delegation's own report closes with them as its subject at oshb:Isa.36.22, while this verse's own wayehi-plus-explicit-subject clause names the king himself as a fresh actor, the same scene-onset construction the surrounding narrative block uses at its own opening seam.

current_row.device_notes: The sackcloth-covering tie is internal to this unit: Hezekiah covers himself at its own onset, וַיִּתְכַּ֣ס בַּשָּׂ֔ק (oshb:Isa.37.1, tier: byte), and the delegation he sends is covered the same way two verses later, מִתְכַּסִּ֖ים בַּשַּׂקִּ֑ים (oshb:Isa.37.2, tier: byte) — the same root in a different stem plus the same noun pluralized, ROOT TIER, cohering the unit from within rather than crossing any seam. A tear-and-garment pair straddles the seam between this unit and the one that follows: the delegation's own torn clothes are named at the close of oshb:Isa.36.22, קְרוּעֵ֣י בְגָדִ֑ים (oshb:Isa.36.22, tier: byte), and Hezekiah tears his own clothes just across the seam at oshb:Isa.37.1, וַיִּקְרַ֖ע אֶת בְּגָדָ֑יו (oshb:Isa.37.1, tier: byte) — the same verbal root and the same noun on both sides, but a different stem and a different pointed form in each case, disclosed at ROOT TIER rather than as a byte-identical recurrence. A parashah SAMEKH mark (single-witness) also falls at oshb:Isa.36.22, the verse immediately before this unit's own onset, corroborating the adopted seam from the tier-3 layer alone: weak, never a driver, and carrying no weight by its absence elsewhere. This unit carries a second koh-amar frame-owner alongside the Assyrian king: the Assyrian king's own herald frame recurs at three prior sites, all three inside chapter 36 — כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ הַגָּדוֹל֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר (oshb:Isa.36.4, tier: byte), כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ (oshb:Isa.36.14, tier: byte), and כֹ֨ה אָמַ֜ר הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֗וּר (oshb:Isa.36.16, tier: byte) — of the book's four-verse royal-messenger set against forty-four divine-frame verses; Hezekiah's own messenger formula at web:Isa.37.3, כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ (oshb:Isa.37.3, tier: byte), is the fourth royal SITE and the second royal frame-OWNER, distinct from the Assyrian sites in chapter 36 and from Isaiah's divine frame that answers it three verses later. That divine frame's own verse, oshb:Isa.37.6, also carries a prefixed speech-commission naming Isaiah's own instruction to the delegation, כֹּ֥ה תֹאמְר֖וּן (oshb:Isa.37.6, tier: byte), one clause ahead of the counted divine frame itself, כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.37.6, tier: byte); the two are distinct objects inside the same verse, and only the second belongs to the frame census.

current_row.boundary_rationale: This unit opens at web:Isa.37.14, “Hezekiah received the letter from the hand of the messengers and read it. Then Hezekiah went up to Yahweh’s house, and spread it before Yahweh.” (web:Isa.37.14), pointed as וַיִּקַּ֨ח חִזְקִיָּ֧הוּ אֶת הַסְּפָרִ֛ים מִיַּ֥ד הַמַּלְאָכִ֖ים וַיִּקְרָאֵ֑הוּ וַיַּ֨עַל֙ בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה וַיִּפְרְשֵׂ֥הוּ חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה (oshb:Isa.37.14, tier: byte); the noun itself is plural, הַסְּפָרִ֛ים (oshb:Isa.37.14, tier: byte), taken up by a verb carrying a singular object suffix — 'the letter' is the English rendering's own singular, not the byte number. Hezekiah's own reception of the documents and his spreading them before Yahweh in the temple open this unit's scene. His own prayer, narrated with its introduction rather than detached from it, opens at oshb:Isa.37.15, וַיִּתְפַּלֵּל֙ חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ אֶל יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Isa.37.15, tier: byte) — the frame this row's whole argument rests on — and runs to its own close at web:Isa.37.20, “Now therefore, Yahweh our God, save us from his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you are Yahweh, even you only.” (web:Isa.37.20), in Hebrew וְעַתָּה֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ הוֹשִׁיעֵ֖נוּ מִיָד֑וֹ וְיֵֽדְעוּ֙ כָּל מַמְלְכ֣וֹת הָאָ֔רֶץ כִּֽי אַתָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה לְבַדֶּֽךָ (oshb:Isa.37.20, tier: byte). Frame and speech stay together here as the default larger unit: the narrated act of prayer and the prayer's own content are a single continuous scene with one participant before Yahweh.
